text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYMEAL SALE - South Korea's Korea Feed Association bought 43,800 tonnes of Indian soybean meal and 4,500 tonnes of Indian rapeseed meal. Position one (22,300 tonnes of soybean meal) from Toepfer at $308.23 a tonne, C&F, for March 17-April 5, with arrival by April 20. Position two (13,000 tonnes of soybean meal) from Toshoku Ltd at $309.50, for March 7-26 with arrival by April 10. Position three (8,500 tonnes of soybean meal and 4,500 tonnes of rapeseed meal) from LG International at $309 for soymeal meal and at $147.50 for rapeseed meal.
SOYMEAL SALE - Thai feed producers bought 20,000 tonnes of optional origin soymeal from South America for February shipment, trade sources said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka is expected to seek on February 6 a total of 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat for February-March shipment, U.S. exporters said.
- The CCC said it was seeking up to 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 soft white wheat, 13.5 pct moisture, for Pakistan. Shipment period was slated for February 20 to March 15.

WHEAT TENDERS - Egypt's main wheat buyer said Tuesday it was back in the market, seeking bids for 50,000 tonnes of Argentine, U.S. or French wheat for loading in March or April. The wheat could be of any variety. The deadline for bids is 8 a.m. local (0600 GMT) on February 1.

- An Algerian official said Algeria seeks to buy 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat between mid-March and the end of April. The official from the Algerian Office Interprofessionnel des Cereales said Algeria would consider durum from the U.S., Canada and Syria. The tender calls for shipments of 50,000 tonnes each for March 16-31, April 1-15 and April 16-30.
CORN TENDER - News was awaited on South Africa's Maize Board's tender for 15,000 tonnes of yellow maize for either export or domestic use.

BARLEY TENDERS - Tunisia launched a tender for 100,000 tonnes of any-origin barley for shipment between May and August -- the first from the region to include new-crop positions, European grain exporters confirmed on Tuesday. The closing date for the tender is January 30.
- Turkey will tender February 3 to export 150,000 tonnes of feed barley and 50,000 tonnes of malting barley for shipment in February and March, traders said.
BARLEY TENDER - News was awaited on Iran's tender January 27 to import 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley, European grain traders said. The barley is for shipment in April.
RICE TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 3.

- Iraq will tender on February 3 for 30,000 tonnes of U.S. long grain rice under Iraq's "food-for-oil" program, U.S. exporters said. The tender is for two equal 15,000 tonne positions for April and May delivery.

SOYBEAN TENDERS - The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association on Tuesday passed on a tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans due to high prices, traders said.

- South Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp invited tenders for 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 soybeans on January 29. Shipment of 20,000 tonnes will be for January 30-February 18 from the U.S. Gulf or February 14-March 5 from the U.S. Pacific Northwest. Shipment of the other 20,000 tonnes will be from the U.S. Gulf February 24-March 15 or from PNW March 11-30.
PALM STEARIN TENDER - Egypt's state Food Industries Co said it sought 10,000 tonnes of Malaysian or Indonesian palm stearin for March delivery. The tender will close 1000 GMT on February 12.

MARKET TALK - The Canadian Wheat Board was not aware of any problems with Canadian wheat destined for India and there has been no contact between the two countries regarding Canadian wheat not meeting contract specifications, a CWB spokesman told Reuters... The State Trading Corp (STC) denied a newspaper report on Tuesday that India had contracted to buy poor quality wheat from Canada without checking for levels of poisonous mycotoxin. "We are totally denying all the allegations. It is baseless," STC director Deepak Prasad told Reuters.
